# Changing Addon Character Name/Realm
## post by Kaldara-2020679 on Jun 5, 2021
Ehiztari <Gentlemen of the Road>
958 posts
50 Tauren Hunter 5380
8
Jun 2021
Over the years I’ve seen a number of posts about how changing a character’s name/realm has caused chaos with regards to some addon settings.
I’ve just completed a name change and found a relatively simple method for making that a smooth transition.

...

You can probably stop reading now.
Also, this will NOT work if your OLD character name is on multiple realms (unless you’re either changing all of them or you don’t mind all of them but the one with the name change getting messed up - like if they’re old toons you keep just for nostalgia).
You’re going to need a tool for making the mass in-file changes. I strongly recommend Notepad++ for this and this guide.
BACK UP YOUR WTF FOLDER FIRST! Both because I might not have caught every possible gotcha here and because you might make an error (either because you didn’t understand or I didn’t make clear some step involved or both).
This first block of instructions assumes you’re only changing (or had forced on you a change in) name.
* Log into the toon under the new name after it’s been changed. You’re not going to play it, you’re just going to force Blizzard and any addons you’re running to create the director(y)(ies) you’ll need.
* Exit the game completely.
* Open File Explorer (assumes Windows here - there’s a Mac equivalent for this but I don’t know what it is - please comment with a note I can include here).
* Locate your …_retail_/WTF/Account/<account name>/<realm name> folder.
* Within that folder you’ll see a folder for every toon you’ve ever had on that server (unless you’ve deleted some of the folders previously). Locate the folder for your character’s _previous_ name and open it.
* Select all/copy all the files and folders in there.
* Back out of that folder.
* Locate the folder for your character’s _new_ name and open it.
* Paste everything from the prior folder into this one replacing all files and folders.
* Close File Explorer and open Notepad++.
* From the file menu, choose “Open File As Workspace” and choose the ACCOUNT NAME folder within your …_retail_/WTF/Account/<account name>/<realm name> path.
* Right click that folder in the workspace area and select “Find In Files…”.
* When the dialog opens, set the first text box to your character’s OLD name and the second text box to your character’s NEW name.
Make sure the “Filters” box reads *.*, the “Search Mode” is normal, “Match whole word only”, “Match case”, “Follow current doc.”, and “In hidden folders” are all unchecked, and “In all sub-folders” is checked.
* Click “Replace in Files”.
If you are not changing servers, that’s it.
If you are changing servers, you’ll need to make a few changes to the above:
* You’ll be copying your old character files from the folder under your old realm, not the new one (fairly obvious, but included for completeness).
* You’ll be copying them into the new character under the new realm (again, a Mr.
Obvious comment, but not everyone sees the obvious when dealing with technical issues).
* You’ll have to chase down any saved data related to your character that includes the name and server name.
Virtually all of these are kept at the global “Saved Variables” level (it’s something to do with ACE2 and the libraries many addons use for storing data - they don’t exactly follow the design intent that Blizzard laid out with how character-specific data should be stored).
* Expand the ACCOUNT LEVEL folder in the workspace area.
* Right click the “SavedVariables” folder and select “Find in Files…”
* In the first text box, type the OLD Realm Name (as far as I know the default in the ACE2 libraries is the proper name “Earthen Ring” rather than “EarthenRing”).
If you find that an addon or two still isn’t behaving, repeat this set of steps with spaces removed from the realm name.
If you still have trouble after this repeat this set of steps on the “SavedVariables” files that are under your REALM and CHARACTER folders (note - this deeper editing should not be necessary - I use WeakAuras 2 and ElvUI and both use ACE2 libraries and both worked just fine without it, but . . .

...

* Double-clicking each of the line numbers shown in that list will bring up the file/line in question and if it relates to your character’s NEW name and OLD realm, correct the realm name (perfectly - accuracy counts here).
A search / replace for “ToonName-Realm Name”, “ToonName - Realm Name”, or the “…RealmName” equivalents won’t likely do the job because some addons store the two separately (ElvUI for one).
Safest to find every instance of your changed toon’s old realm name and make the changes manually as you go, which will sometimes involve moving things around in tables a bit.

excerpts:
# Pages
## AceDB-3.0 Tutorial
**AceDB-3.0** is a library to manage the SavedVariables of an addon.
It offers profile management, smart defaults and child-databases for modules.

## Getting Started
First, we need to make sure that we have the table we want to use to store our DB in defined in the addons .toc, like this.
```
## SavedVariables: AceDBExampleDB
```

...

## Data Types
* **char** Character-specific data. Every character has its own database.
* **realm** Realm-specific data. All of the players characters on the same realm share this database.
* **class** Class-specific data. All of the players characters of the same class share this database.
* **race** Race-specific data.
All of the players characters of the same race share this database.
* **faction** Faction-specific data. All of the players characters of the same faction share this database.
* **factionrealm** Faction and realm specific data. All of the players characters on the same realm and of the same faction share this database.
* **global** Global Data. All characters on the same account share this database.
* **profile** Profile-specific data. All characters using the same profile share this database. The user can control which profile should be used.
You can use all of those at the same time
```
local charName = UnitName ( " player" ) 

 function MyAddon : OnInitialize () 
  self . db = LibStub ( " AceDB-3.0" ): New ( " MyAddonDB" ) 
  self . db . char . money = GetMoney () 
  self . db . global . money [ charName ] = GetMoney () 
 end
```

# TOC format
`.toc` files contain information about the addon (e.g. addon name, addon description, addon saved variables). They also specify the loading order for the addon's `.lua` and `.xml` files. A `.toc` file is mandatory for an addon.
The filename of the `.toc` file must match the folder it's inside, otherwise the `.toc` file won't load.

## Rules
The `.toc` file and folder name must match. For example `..\Interface\AddOns\MyAddon\MyAddon.toc`
The `.toc` file can optionally have the following elements:
* Metadata as `## Directive : Value`
* Comments as `# this is a comment`
* A list of files as `myFile.xml` or `subfolder\myFile.lua`

...

## Saved variables
### LoadSavedVariablesFirst
`1` if SavedVariables file(s) should be loaded before all script files for this addon.

### SavedVariables
Variables saved in `WTF/[account]/SavedVariables` .
```
## SavedVariables : MyAddOnNameFoo, MyAddOnNameBar
```

### SavedVariablesPerCharacter
Variables saved in `WTF/[account]/[server]/[character]/SavedVariables` .
```
## SavedVariablesPerCharacter : MyAddOnNameAnotherVariable
```

...

## Restricted
### SavedVariablesMachine
List of global variable names to be persisted across all accounts on the same machine.

...

## Patch changes
### Modern
* The War Within **Patch 11.1.5 (2025-04-22):**
+ Added support for per-file conditional directives and variables.
+ Added the `LoadSavedVariablesFirst` field.
+ `AllowLoadGameType` is now usable by insecure addons.
* The War Within **Patch 11.1.0 (2025-02-25):** Added the `Category` and `Group` fields.
